summary: This clipped documentation page describes the GET_CONFIG method for Snowflake budgets, which returns budget configuration properties. It lists the returned columns (notification channel, notification email, last notification time, spend limit, mute flag, budget type, and account-budget-only activation fields), the access control requirements for custom and account budgets, and two example CALL statements. The feature is not available for trial accounts.
one_line: Snowflake documentation for the budget GET_CONFIG method, which returns a budget's notification, spend limit, and activation configuration.
key_facts: The GET_CONFIG method is invoked with the syntax <budget_name>!GET_CONFIG().
The GET_CONFIG feature is currently not available for Trial Accounts.
The NOTIFICATION_EMAIL column returns budget notification email address(es) as a comma-separated list when there is more than one.
The LAST_NOTIFICATION_TIME column is a UTC timestamp of when the last email notification was sent.
The SPEND_LIMIT column gives the budget's spending limit in credits.
The NOTIFICATION_MUTE_FLAG column is TRUE if email notifications are muted for the budget.
BUDGET_TYPE valid values are ACCOUNT_ROOT_BUDGET or USER_BUDGET.
IS_ACTIVE is TRUE if the account budget has been activated and is only available for the account budget.
ACTIVATION_TIMESTAMP is a TIMESTAMP_TZ giving when the account budget was activated and is only available for the account budget.
To view results for a custom budget, a role needs the USAGE privilege on the database and schema containing the budget instance.
Viewing results for the account budget requires a specific application role described in the budgets documentation.
An example call for a custom budget is CALL budget_db.budget_schema.my_budget!GET_CONFIG();.
An example call for the account budget is CALL snowflake.local.account_root_budget!GET_CONFIG();.
